variables.title: Variables
variables.sensitiveLeakWarning: Redaction masks only verbatim occurrences in output. A command that transforms the secret (base64, hashing, partial echo) before printing may still leak it — this is defence-in-depth, not a guarantee.
variables.helpTooltip:
Reference variables in the script, args, working directory, or env values with ${name}.

Syntax:
  ${name}            — substituted from the value at runtime or from the default.
  ${name:default}    — inline default; used if no value is provided.
  ${name:}           — defaults to the empty string.
  $$                 — a literal $.

Name regex: [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*

Variables without a default trigger a prompt before each run.
Mark a variable as Sensitive to mask its value in events and logs.
Values are NOT shell-quoted — quote "${var}" in your script if needed.

processCapture.title: Recorder
processCapture.subtitle: Capture the commands that other apps launch under the hood, and turn them into ProcMix commands.
processCapture.explainer: The Recorder watches the programs (processes) your computer starts — not your mouse clicks or what you type. While it's running, do something in another app that kicks off work (open a file, build, sync, export…); the command lines of any processes that app launches show up below, ready to save.
processCapture.empty: No processes captured yet. Press Start, then trigger some work in another app — the command lines of the processes it launches will appear here.
processCapture.emptyRecording: Recording process launches… Trigger some work in another app (build, sync, export…) to capture the command lines it runs.
processCapture.unsupported: Process recording is not yet implemented on this operating system. It is currently available on Windows and Linux — macOS support is planned.
processCapture.startFailed: Couldn't start recording. On Windows it uses an ETW trace session that needs administrator rights — run ProcMix as administrator and try again.
processCapture.requiresPrivilege: Couldn't start recording. On Linux the kernel process connector needs the CAP_NET_ADMIN capability. Grant it once with: sudo setcap cap_net_admin+ep <path-to-procmix>, then restart ProcMix.

consent.title: Enable Process Capture?
consent.message: ProcMix will observe processes started on this computer while recording is on, and show their command lines so you can turn them into commands. Command lines may contain passwords or tokens — these are masked before display and are never saved unless you choose to save a command. The raw capture log is kept in memory only and is never written to disk.

manual.label: How to call the API
manual.body:
Run saved commands and workflows over HTTP.

Auth: send the access token on every request:
  Authorization: Bearer <token>

Run a command (by its API slug or id):
  curl -X POST http://{{host}}:{{port}}/api/command/<slug>/run \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Run a workflow:
  curl -X POST http://{{host}}:{{port}}/api/workflow/<slug>/run \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Pass variables (and wait for the result):
  curl -X POST "http://{{host}}:{{port}}/api/command/<slug>/run?wait=true" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"variables":{"name":"value"}}'

List what is exposed (returns each id + slug):
  GET /api/commands   GET /api/workflows

No slug? Run by id instead — take the id from the list above and use it in place of the slug:
  POST /api/command/<id>/run

Only commands/workflows with the API toggle enabled are reachable. Without ?wait the call returns 202 immediately; with ?wait=true it blocks and returns the exit code/status.
